title: Union-Find
summary: Tracking groups that merge - the disjoint-set problem, a forest of parent pointers, find and union, union by size or rank, path compression, the nearly constant inverse-Ackermann bound, counting components and component sizes, and applications such as connectivity, image regions, percolation and (in lesson 5.04) Kruskal's algorithm.

cards.a:
The root of x's tree, which represents its whole set

Two elements are in the same set exactly when they have the same root.

cards.q: What does union by size do?
cards.a:
Attaches the smaller tree's root under the larger tree's root

A node only gets deeper when its tree at least doubles, so depths stay O(log n).

cards.q: unite(a, b) returns false because a and b are already connected. In a graph built edge by edge, what does that tell you?
cards.a:
The edge (a, b) closes a cycle

There was already a path between a and b; the new edge makes a second one.
